prompt: Write an expression for "$5$ less than twice a number $n$".
hint: This phrase has two parts. Work out which part is built first and which part is done to it afterwards.

hints.text: This phrase has two parts. Work out which part is built first and which part is done to it afterwards.
"Twice a number" is $2n$. "$5$ less than" that amount means you take $5$ away from $2n$, not the other way round.
Start with $2n$ and subtract $5$, so the expression is $2n - 5$.

explanation: "Twice a number $n$" means two times $n$, which is written $2n$.
"$5$ less than" an amount means that amount made smaller by $5$, so the $5$ is subtracted from $2n$.
The expression is $2n - 5$. It is not $5 - 2n$, because the words come in the opposite order to the symbols.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test with a real number
steps: Let $n = 10$. Twice 10 is 20, and 5 less than 20 is 15.
Check the expressions: $2(10) - 5 = 15$ works, but $5 - 2(10) = -15$ does not.
